releases.name: Kelabo 1.1.1
releases.body:
A patch release with one fix: a scheduled kelabo now reaches the **host's own calendar**, not only the invitees'.

## Fix

### The host gets their own calendar copy (#17, #18)
Every scheduling mail skipped the host. A scheduled kelabo reached each invitee's Outlook, Google or Apple calendar, but never the host's. The host now gets a mail of their own:

- **On scheduling, and when the time changes:** an iCalendar `METHOD:PUBLISH` entry, carrying the join link and the invitation link to share. A title-only edit mails nobody, which matches the rule for invitees.
- **On cancelling:** a `METHOD:CANCEL` on the same event, which removes it from the host's calendar.

Unlike the invitee mail, this one is `PUBLISH`, not `REQUEST`, and has no Accept/Decline buttons. The host is the event's organizer, and Outlook does not add a `REQUEST` addressed to its own organizer to the calendar. The copy uses the invitations' UID, so a reschedule moves the same entry instead of adding a second one.

If the host copy fails to send, the schedule still succeeds. The API response reports the outcome as `hostCopy: { sent, reason? }`. Invitee mail is unchanged.

## Upgrading

```bash
git pull
make deploy env=<env>   # or `make backend env=<env>`: only the REST API Lambda changed
```

There are no infrastructure or configuration changes.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/kelabome/kelabo/compare/1.1.0...1.1.1

releases.name: Kelabo 1.1.0
releases.body:
Kelabo 1.1.0 is about finding people, organisations that are more than one
domain, and an assistant that is yours to choose. It also fixes a board leak,
hardens sign-in mail, and makes the gateway deploy refuse to guess.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Kelabo is transparent by design.** Everything said with the mic on is
> transcribed and shown to the whole room. The assistant answers only onto a
> board everyone sees, and an attached coding agent is announced. Every
> kelabo ends as minutes and a searchable record. It is built for teams that
> want fair, open communication; if yours is not ready for that, Kelabo is
> not the right choice. The README now says so at the top.

## Highlights

### Your organisation's directory, imported (#8)
Before this release, nobody could be found by name until they had signed in
once. `/admin` → **Directory** now takes the people list your mail system
already exports: Entra "Download users", Microsoft 365 "Export users", Google
Workspace's user download, Outlook or Google contacts, a hand-made
`Name,Email` sheet, or a pasted recipient list.
- Search matches names and addresses typo-tolerantly: prefixes, one slip,
  transpositions, initials, and accents folded.
- Invite fields, journey accessors and Contacts all use it. Ring pickers
  still offer only people who have signed in.
- An import **replaces** the tenant's directory, which is how leavers drop
  out. An import that would remove more than half of it is refused until you
  confirm. Preview shows what would be added, renamed and removed, and which
  rows were skipped, by line number.

### One organisation, several email domains (#15, fixes #14)
`emailDomainAliases` (in `kelabo.json`, or published from `/admin` →
Access) lists the organisation's other domains. People at any of them sign in
as colleagues in one tenant. `allowedEmailDomain` stays the primary. If
people at a domain already had accounts before it became an alias,
`rest-api/scripts/restamp-tenant.mjs` moves what they created.

A public mailbox domain (gmail.com, outlook.com…) is never an organisation.
Under open registration it gets no people search, presence, ringing,
favourites, tenant-wide kelabo list or organisation-wide journeys.

### Model- and supplier-independent assistant
The docs and template no longer name a default LLM supplier. Kelabo speaks
the Anthropic Messages API and the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API, so
the deployment chooses both the model and who serves it. The docs explain why
the second choice is a privacy decision. The template's example is now
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash served by DeepInfra, in place of DeepSeek's own API.
Your deployment's model is unchanged unless you change it.

Each assistant conversation also sends its own prompt-cache key to providers
that route by key (OpenAI, DeepInfra). A long kelabo's growing transcript is
then billed at the cache-read rate.

### Coding agents in the README
The README now has a dedicated section on attaching your own Claude Code or
opencode session to a kelabo:
- **before** the meeting, it posts its findings from your repository;
- **during** the meeting, it answers onto the board;
- **afterwards**, it builds what was agreed, with the whole discussion
  already in its context.

## Also new
- **Calendar invitations** arrive with Accept/Decline and a join link (#9).
- **Removing a board post**: the host or the post's author can remove it, and
  every open board drops it at once (#11).
- **Ending a kelabo** shows a please-wait dialog while the record and minutes
  are prepared, with the option to leave (#12).
- **Journeys** (#16):
  - Public journeys are now followed explicitly. Only followers, the lead and
    people a message mentions are notified or badged.
  - A private question leaves no timeline row and no counts.
  - Askers can remove their own questions.
  - Reading a leg clears its badge at once, in every tab.
- **Credentials**: `make credentials-import` fills or refreshes every
  credential slot from one gitignored

releases.name: Kelabo 1.0.0
releases.body:
Kelabo is live rooms with transcription, an AI assistant that answers *into the
meeting*, minutes written for you, and a searchable archive of everything your
team decided. This is the first release: the whole product, MIT licensed,
deployable into your own AWS account.

## The two ideas

**A kelabo** is one live room — conference audio, live transcript, chat, and a
shared board the assistant posts to. When it ends it is archived: transcript,
board and generated minutes, all searchable.

**A journey** carries memory *between* kelabos. Link related rooms and the next
one starts with the previous ones' minutes, pinned notes, documents and running
description — visible to the people in the room and injected into the
assistant's context, so it answers from what the project already decided.

## What's in it

- **Live rooms** with conference audio, camera and screen share. Two transports:
  `sfu` (Cloudflare Realtime, scales) or `mesh` — a "secure kelabo" where media
  stays peer-to-peer and no server can decrypt it.
- **Live transcription** streamed browser → Deepgram or Soniox **directly**.
  Audio never touches Kelabo's infrastructure, self-hosted or hosted; the server
  receives text.
- **An assistant in the room** that answers while the question still matters,
  onto a shared board. Silent by default; `@kelabo` addresses it directly.
- **Minutes and a searchable archive** of every ended kelabo.
- **Journeys** — documents, pinned board notes, named legs, and an append-only
  Q&A history generated from every linked kelabo's minutes.
- **Scheduling, invitations, contacts and presence** — including ringing someone
  into a huddle straight from Contacts.
- **Bring your own coding agent.** `npm i -g @kelabome/agents` attaches your own
  opencode or Claude Code session to a kelabo: it hears the transcript and posts
  to the board, and every permission prompt stays in your terminal. Kelabo never
  runs your agent — it hands it a channel.
- **An admin console, so day two is not a deploy.** `/admin` publishes the model,
  the transcription engine, the mail transport, every rate limit and TTL, and
  holds the supplier keys — live in seconds, versioned, with an author and a note
  on every change. Only what CloudFormation reads at synth still needs a deploy.
- **Everything optional degrades, nothing jams.** No STT key? The room is typed
  messages and calls. No LLM? No assistant surface at all — not a broken one. No
  Cloudflare credentials? Peer-to-peer calling still works.

## Running it

Self-hosting needs an AWS account, a Route 53 hosted zone, an STT provider key
(Soniox or Deepgram), an LLM provider key, and SES production access for sign-in
mail. The [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md) walks from an empty account
to `kelabo.mycompany.com`; from then on upgrades are `git pull && make deploy`.

Or use the hosted service at [kelabo.me](https://kelabo.me) — identical
functionality, run at cost.

```bash
make bootstrap        # npm install in every package
make test             # every package's test suite, no AWS needed
make help             # everything is a make target
Where to read
- ARCHITECTURE.md (ARCHITECTURE.md) — the overview
- docs/ (docs/) — numbered design docs: transcript lifecycle, agent
orchestration, conference RTC, journeys, operational configuration
- docs/self-hosting.md (docs/self-hosting.md) — empty AWS account to a running
deployment
MIT licensed.
